subject: History
description: Governors-General & Viceroys of India — key achievements + events

questions.stem: The FIRST Governor-General of India was:
questions.explanation: Warren Hastings — first Governor-General of Bengal / India (1774-85) under the Regulating Act 1773. Clive was first Governor (not GG) of Bengal post-Plassey. Lord Cornwallis (1786-93) introduced Permanent Settlement. Dalhousie — Doctrine of Lapse.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The FIRST VICEROY of India (post-1858 transfer of power to the Crown) was:
questions.explanation: Lord Canning — last Governor-General (1856-58) and first VICEROY (1858-62). Implemented Queen Victoria's Proclamation. Also established universities (1857). Lord Mountbatten — LAST Viceroy (1947).
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Match the VICEROY with the EVENT. A. Lord Curzon.  B. Lord Hardinge II.  C. Lord Chelmsford.  D. Lord Mountbatten. List-II: 1. Partition of Bengal (1905).  2. Shift of capital to Delhi (1911).  3. Rowlatt Act + Jallianwala (1919).  4. Partition of India (1947).
questions.explanation: Curzon (1899-1905) — Bengal partition. Hardinge II (1910-16) — capital shift to Delhi, 1911. Chelmsford (1916-21) — Jallianwala Bagh under his watch (though the massacre was Dyer's action; GoI Act 1919 = Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms). Mountbatten (1947) — Partition + Independence, last Viceroy.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Lord CURZON is remembered primarily for:

options.option_text: Partitioning Bengal (1905), setting up ASI, police reforms
Introducing the Government of India Act 1935

questions.explanation: Curzon (1899-1905) — Partition of Bengal (1905, reason given: administrative efficiency; real motive: divide-and-rule); set up Archaeological Survey of India (1861 origin, Curzon revived with ASI Act); Police Reforms (1902-03). Dismissed for clashing with Lord Kitchener.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The 'PERMANENT SETTLEMENT' (1793) of Bengal was introduced by:
questions.explanation: Cornwallis (1786-93) — Permanent Settlement of Bengal, Bihar, Orissa, 1793. Fixed land revenue for zamindars permanently (10/11 to British, 1/11 to zamindar). Also introduced the Civil Service (separated revenue/judicial). Third Anglo-Mysore war under him.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: SATI was abolished in 1829 under Governor-General:
questions.explanation: Lord William Bentinck (GG 1828-35) — Regulation XVII of 1829 declared Sati illegal. Roused by Raja Ram Mohan Roy's campaigning. Also abolished Thuggee (with William Sleeman); English introduced as medium of higher education (Macaulay Minute, 1835).
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The LAST Viceroy of India was:
questions.explanation: Lord Mountbatten — last Viceroy (21 March 1947 to 15 August 1947), continued as first Governor-General of independent India (August 1947 to June 1948). C. Rajagopalachari — second and LAST GG of independent India (June 1948 to 26 January 1950, when GG post ended and Republic began).
